newsitem.title: ITALY: Joking Pope appears in public after surgery.
newsitem.headline: Joking Pope appears in public after surgery.

text.p: Pope John Paul, joking about his temporary exile in a hospital, appeared in public for the first time in a week on Sunday after surgery to remove his appendix.

"I cordially greet all those people here in what has become the third Vatican," he said from his window at the Gemelli hospital, prompting cheers and laughter from the crowd of some 2,000 people in a courtyard below.
"The first Vatican is St Peter's, the second is (the summer residence at) Castelgandolfo. The Gemelli hospital has become number three," he said.

The 76-year-old Polish Pontiff entered the hospital a week ago and on Tuesday doctors removed his appendix. They said the operation was a success and confirmed there had been no recurrence of a colon tumour removed in 1992.

It is the sixth time the Pope has been admitted to the Gemelli hospital since his election in 1978. The first was for emergency surgery to save his life in 1981 after Turkish gunman Mehmet Ali Agca shot him in St Peter's Square.
The Pope appeared alert and in relatively good form during the appearance at the window, which lasted more than five minutes.
"Now I have to go back to my bedroom...I hope that next week we can do this from the first Vatican, St Peter's Square," he said. Many in the crowd were Polish countrymen.
He thanked doctors who had treated him and said he felt close to all other patients in the sprawling Catholic teaching hospital in Rome's northeastern outskirts.
He appeared shortly after the crowd and other pilgrims in St Peter's Square at the Vatican heard a recorded message in which he thanked those who had prayed for him.
In the recorded message, however, the Pontiff sounded much weaker. It was taped either on Saturday afternoon or Sunday morning.
In it, he called the hospital, a "place of suffering and prayer".

Noting that on Wednesday he will mark the 18th anniversary of his election and on November 1 his 50th year as a priest, the Pope said hospitalisation had made him better understand the value of his service to God and the Church.

The Pontiff is expected to leave the hospital either on Monday or Tuesday. Doctors have said he has made a very good recovery from the surgery but several of them have openly suggested that he slow down, travel less and rest more.
But there are signs already that he will disobey them, as he has after past hospitalisations.
Vatican officials say the Pope plans to celebrate his first public mass at the Vatican to mark a religious holiday on October 27. This will require him to stand for at least three hours.
But aides say he will most likely begin short audiences even earlier.
They say the Pope is keen to be in good shape for November 1, when he has invited priests from around the world also celebrating the 50th anniversary of their ordination to come to Rome.
The Pope is due to make four overseas trips next year, including to Poland, the Czech Republic, France and Brazil.
